question: When does a reference actually hold a mapped name?
question_corrected_before_measuring: Round 009 framed this as a population RATE. Reading PropertyLinkBase::_updateElementReference shows the fraction of populated references in any model is a function of what that model references, so a rate would describe the fixture. The measurable thing is the rule.
prediction_from_source_before_measuring: A reference holds a mapped name iff the feature it points at has an element map that resolves the subname. Population follows the target, not the consumer.
prediction_outcome: Confirmed exactly, in both directions, on all three target kinds.

durability.verdict: durable - not transient state that a change wipes

fallback_for_unmapped_target.what_is_stored: the index name alone (old='Face2'), with an empty mapped name
fallback_for_unmapped_target.classification: SILENT - the reference works and nothing marks it as resting on a weaker identity. The '?' missing marker appears only when a reference BREAKS, not when it is stored without a map.

controls.positive: populated names observed in the same run (Cut, Fillet), so the emptiness reported for Box is a measurement and not an untested probe
controls.negative: N5 asserts the deliberately wrong expectation that a Cut reference is empty; reported as false, so the harness distinguishes the two states

verification_pass: Cut map_size=50 matches round 007's corrected probe exactly - independent reproduction, different harness.
Fillet map_size 56 here vs 32 in round 007 is explained by the fixture: round 007 filleted a Box, this round fillets a Cut.
The hash segment varies between tests but is identical across three readings inside one document, consistent with it encoding the object tag. Stated as the plausible reading, not proven.
The fillet's mapped name chains two hashes, corroborating round 004's reading that the naming grammar encodes the generator.
not_reportable: Any population rate. The fixture chooses the targets, so a rate would measure the fixture.
caveats: Part workbench only; PartDesign still cannot be run here.
Cross-session stability of the hash segment is untested - within one document it is stable, and round 007's M3 saw a fillet survive saveAs/reopen, but that is not the same measurement.
